title: Assignment changes a stored value
meaning: A Python name points to a value. Assignment first works out the right-hand side using the values stored now. Then it makes the name on the left point to that result. It is a step that runs once, not a formula that stays connected.
picture: Draw a before-and-after table for distance = 2, step = 3, then distance = distance + step. Keep the printed output in a separate column.
predict: After that update, step is assigned 10. Does distance automatically become 12?
steps: Before the update: distance is 2 and step is 3.
Work out the right side: 2 + 3 gives 5. Store 5 in distance.
Assigning 10 to step later does not run the earlier line again. distance stays 5.
answer: The result is 5. A stored number is not a live spreadsheet formula. When an input changes, you must calculate again yourself.
transfer: Change the update to distance = step + step. Before running it, say which old value no longer matters.
tr: Atama önce sağ tarafı hesaplar, sonra adı sonuca bağlar. Girdi değişince önceki satır kendiliğinden yeniden çalışmaz.

title: Text, number and display are three different things
meaning: The text "10.05", the number 10.05 and a formatted display are not the same thing. Conversion turns text into a number so you can do arithmetic. Formatting makes a result easy to read. Neither step checks that a measurement is correct.
picture: Draw a pipeline: input text → number → decision → display. Write millimetres next to the number in your explanation. Python does not know the unit from the variable name.
predict: The limit is 10.05 mm, inclusive. A two-decimal display shows 10.05. Should a reading of 10.051 pass because of that display?
steps: The text "10.051" becomes the number 10.051.
Compare the unrounded value with 10.05: it is above the limit.
A formatted display can show 10.05, but the stored value is still 10.051.
answer: It fails under this exact-value teaching rule. Rounding the display must not quietly change the decision. A real inspection policy may also need measurement uncertainty. That is a separate question from formatting.
transfer: Compare "12" + "3" with 12 + 3. Explain why the same symbol can join text or add numbers.
tr: Metin, sayı ve biçimlendirilmiş çıktı farklıdır. Gösterimde yuvarlama, karar için kullanılan değeri sessizce değiştirmemelidir.

title: A condition writes down a rule and its limits
meaning: A Boolean expression answers one exact yes/no question. An if/elif chain picks the first branch whose test is true. Separate if statements ask separate questions. Write the operating rule in words before you choose the syntax.
picture: Draw a temperature number line. Mark the accepted range 10 ≤ temperature ≤ 40. Then draw a second gate for guard_closed. The machine may run only if both gates pass.
predict: Classify temperatures 9, 10, 40 and 41 with a closed guard. What changes when the guard is open?
steps: With a closed guard, 10 and 40 pass. Both end points are included.
9 and 41 fail the range test.
With an open guard, every temperature fails. The and condition needs both parts to be true.
answer: The condition means “inside the range AND guard closed.” With or, the machine could run when only one requirement holds. This is a logic exercise, not a complete machine-safety controller.
transfer: Change the rule so the upper end point is not included. Find exactly one comparison that must change. Then write one test that catches the change.
tr: Önce işletme kuralını ve sınırlarını çiz. and bütün koşulları ister; or yalnızca birinin sağlanmasıyla doğru olabilir.

title: An accumulator remembers what has been processed
meaning: A loop repeats the same update many times. After every pass, the accumulator has a clear meaning: total is the sum of the values seen so far. That meaning tells you the starting value. It also tells you where the update line belongs.
picture: Trace the three samples 4, 7 and 2. Draw one row per pass with columns: current sample, previous total and new total.
predict: What does the program remember if total = 0 is moved inside the loop?
steps: Before any sample: total = 0, the sum of no values.
After 4, then 7, then 2: total becomes 4, 11, 13.
Resetting inside the loop gives 4, 7, 2 instead. Each earlier sample is erased.
answer: The intended answer is 13. A repeated line is useful only if its update keeps the meaning of total correct.
transfer: Replace the addition with count = count + 1. Explain why the result becomes 3, not 13. For a nested loop, trace one complete inner loop before the outer loop moves on.
tr: Toplam değişkeni işlenen kısmın toplamını tutar. Her turda sıfırlamak önceki veriyi siler; saymak ile toplamak farklıdır.

title: A while loop needs progress, not only a condition
meaning: A while loop checks its condition before every pass. The condition says when to keep going. An update inside the loop must move the values toward stopping. A correct condition alone does not guarantee that the loop ends.
picture: Draw a cycle: test attempts < 3 → do one attempt → increase attempts → test again. Mark the exit where the test is false.
predict: Start with attempts = 0. How many attempts happen? What if continue runs before the increment every time?
steps: The tests at attempts 0, 1 and 2 are true. Each completed pass adds 1 to attempts.
At attempts 3 the test is false, so no fourth attempt starts.
If every pass skips the update, attempts stays 0. The loop never ends.
answer: There are three attempts in the first version. Every path that continues must make progress, or another stopping rule must exist. break leaves the loop at once; continue skips the rest of the current pass.
transfer: Start at attempts = 3 and predict whether the body runs. Running zero times is different from running once and then checking.
tr: Koşul devam etmeyi söyler; güncelleme bitişe ilerlemeyi sağlar. continue güncellemeyi atlarsa döngü sonsuza gidebilir.

title: A list is an object, and names can share it
meaning: Assigning a list to a second name does not copy its elements. Both names can point to the same list, and that list can change. A copy creates a new outer list. It does not automatically copy lists nested inside.
picture: Draw raw → [3, 1, 3] and view pointing to the same box after view = raw. Draw a second box instead after view = raw.copy().
predict: Run view.sort() in each version. Which version keeps the original order in raw?
steps: With an alias, sorting the shared list makes both names show [1, 3, 3].
With a copy of this flat list of numbers, raw stays [3, 1, 3] and view becomes [1, 3, 3].
The repeated 3 is still a separate observation. Removing it changes the dataset.
answer: The copied version keeps the order in raw. Sorting in place changes the list and returns None, not the sorted list. “Same object?” and “same displayed values?” are different questions.
transfer: Replace the elements with nested lists. Explain why a shallow copy can still share an inner list. Then try changing an inner list.
tr: İki ad aynı listeyi gösterebilir. Kopya dış listeyi ayırır; iç içe nesneler sığ kopyada ortak kalabilir.

title: A key finds a value; a missing key is an event
meaning: A dictionary maps each key to one value. Reading d[key] finds the value without a loop. Keys keep the order in which they were added. A key that was never added does not give zero or an empty value. d[key] raises KeyError, and d.get(key) returns None unless you give a default.
picture: Draw factors = {'T1': 1.02, 'P1': 1.10} as two labelled boxes. Write the requests factors['P1'], factors['H1'] and factors.get('H1', 1.0) beside them and mark which one finds a box.
predict: After factors['T2'] = 0.98 is added, in what order does for key in factors visit the keys? What does factors['H1'] do?
steps: factors['P1'] finds the box labelled P1 and gives 1.10; no comparison loop runs.
Adding T2 appends it after P1, so the loop visits T1, P1, T2 in insertion order.
factors['H1'] finds no box and raises KeyError. factors.get('H1', 1.0) returns 1.0 and does not add H1 to the dictionary.
answer: The order is T1, P1, T2, and factors['H1'] stops the program. A default from get() is a decision you made, not data the dictionary had. A tuple such as ('T1', 21.5) is a fixed record. It can be unpacked into names. Because it cannot change, it can also be a key.
transfer: Replace the string keys with (row, col) tuples for a grid. Explain why a list [row, col] cannot be used as a key before trying it.
tr: Sözlükte anahtar değeri bulur; eklenme sırası korunur. Olmayan anahtar `[]` ile KeyError verir, `get()` ise varsayılan döndürür. Demet değiştirilemeyen küçük bir kayıttır.

title: Parsing splits a message into named pieces
meaning: String processing turns one text message into named pieces. Splitting finds the separators. Conversion reads one piece as a number. A successful conversion does not prove that the fields or units mean what the program expects.
picture: Use the simple teaching format "T1,23.5,C". Draw three labelled boxes: sensor, reading text, unit. Keep the raw message while you take the pieces out.
predict: Would "T1,,C" mean zero? Would "T1,23.5,F" describe the same temperature?
steps: Split the normal line into T1, 23.5 and C.
Check that the number field is present. Convert only that field.
Keep the unit with the number. The same number with F means a different temperature from C.
answer: An empty field is missing data, not zero. A wrong unit needs a written rule. Simple splitting works only for this restricted format. Fields with quoted commas need the CSV tools we study later.
transfer: Add a fourth field, or remove the unit. Write the expected rejection or handling rule before you change the parser.
tr: Parçalama alanları bulur; dönüşüm sayıyı yorumlar. Boş alan sıfır değildir, birim de verinin anlamının parçasıdır.

title: A function returns a value to its caller
meaning: A function call does its work with the arguments it receives. return hands a value back to the caller. print only sends text to the screen. A function can print a correct-looking number and still return None.
picture: Draw an arrow from the argument 20 into a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit function. Draw an arrow carrying 68 back to result. Put printed text in a separate output box.
predict: If the function only prints 68, can its caller use result + 1 as if result were 68?
steps: The argument 20 is stored in the local parameter.
The expression 20 × 9 / 5 + 32 gives 68.
return passes 68 to the caller. print alone shows it on screen, and the function then returns None.
answer: The print-only version cannot give the number to the next calculation. Describe a function by its inputs, its returned value and its side effects, not by what appears on the screen.
transfer: Call the conversion twice with different inputs. Explain why each call should use its argument, not a global measurement stored earlier.
tr: print ekrana yazar; return değeri çağırana verir. Görünen çıktı ile sonraki hesaplamada kullanılacak değer farklıdır.

title: Scope finds names; mutation changes objects
meaning: A function can give a local name a new value without changing the caller’s name. But a parameter can point to the caller’s list. Changing that shared list changes what the caller sees. “Local variable” does not mean “private copy of every object.”
picture: Draw a box for the caller and a box for the function. In each box, draw a name pointing to one list [2, 4]. Compare adding an element to that list with pointing the local name at a new list.
predict: Which changes the caller’s list: values.append(6), or values = [6] inside the function?
steps: append changes the shared list, so the caller sees [2, 4, 6].
The assignment values = [6] points the local name at a new list.
The caller still has its original list unless the function returns the new one and the caller stores it.
answer: The first operation changes shared data. The second only changes which list the local name points to. When you build a reusable library, write down which functions change their inputs. Pass each sensor’s settings as arguments.
transfer: Use the same helper with two sensor datasets in different orders. Predict which hidden global value could make the result depend on call order.
tr: Kapsam adın nerede bulunduğunu belirler; mutasyon nesneyi değiştirir. Yerel parametre çağıranın nesnesini paylaşabilir.

title: Invalid data is not the same as zero
meaning: Error handling must keep the meaning of the valid readings. A failed conversion, a nonfinite number and an out-of-range reading each need their own handling. Replacing them with zero invents measurements that never happened.
picture: Trace four inputs: "0", "20", "missing" and "nan". Check conversion, then finiteness, then the allowed range. Only then add a value to the summary.
predict: Suppose missing data becomes zero. How does the average of the valid readings 0 and 20 change?
steps: With only the two valid readings, total = 20 and count = 2, giving mean 10.
Replacing one missing value with zero makes count 3 and gives about 6.67.
A float conversion of "nan" succeeds. The result still needs a finiteness check.
answer: Zero is valid when the sensor rules allow it. Missing data is not a zero reading. Catch the relevant exception, and record or report the failure. Decide what to do when every row is invalid, without dividing by zero.
transfer: Change every row to invalid data. Write the report’s no-data message before running the program.
tr: Eksik veriyi sıfır yapmak ölçüm uydurur ve ortalamayı değiştirir. Dönüşüm, sonluluk ve aralık denetimleri ayrı adımlardır.

title: A saved file must be readable again
meaning: Writing text to a file keeps it after the program ends. A good report keeps enough structure to be read back with the same meaning. Formatting, separators, quoting and file mode all affect that.
picture: Draw memory → writer → file bytes → reader → rebuilt records. Put a sensor label that contains a comma in one field. This shows the difference between simple splitting and CSV parsing.
predict: Will splitting every line at every comma correctly rebuild a quoted field that contains a comma? What happens when a second run uses write mode?
steps: A CSV-aware writer quotes fields when needed. A CSV-aware reader rebuilds them.
A plain split on commas treats the comma inside a quoted field as one more separator.
Write mode replaces an existing file. Append mode adds content, and careless use can duplicate rows or headers.
answer: Test a write-then-read round trip. Close the file, then inspect it. Equal rebuilt records show that the file stored the data correctly. They do not prove that the original measurements were right.
transfer: Run the export twice into a temporary file. Decide whether you want replacement or accumulation. Then check for duplicated headers.
tr: Dosyaya yazmak veriyi saklar. CSV tırnaklaması ve dosya modu anlamı korumalı; yazdığını yeniden okuyarak denetle.

title: An array operation applies to every element at once
meaning: np.array(temps) stores a table with a shape of rows × columns. An expression such as a * 0.001 or a > 24.0 is applied to every element. No loop is written. A mask is an array of True/False with the same shape as the data. axis=0 collapses the rows into one value per column.
picture: Draw [[22.1, 21.8], [24.5, 23.0], [25.2, 23.5]] as three rows and two columns. Beside it draw the mask a > 24.0 with the same shape.
predict: How many True cells does the mask have? What does np.mean(a, axis=0) return: two values or three?
steps: Row 0: 22.1 and 21.8 are both False.
Row 1: 24.5 is True, 23.0 is False; row 2: 25.2 is True, 23.5 is False.
axis=0 collapses the three rows, so the mean has two values, one per column.
answer: The mask has two True cells, both in column 0. The mean has two values: 23.93 and 22.77. mask.sum() gives 2 and a[mask] gives [24.5, 25.2]. Every element was tested by one expression.
transfer: Change the comparison to >= 24.5 and predict the count. Then compute the mean with axis=1 and explain why three values appear.
tr: Bir dizi işlemi her elemana aynı anda uygulanır. Şekil satır × sütun sayısıdır; maske aynı şekilde True/False dizisidir ve axis=0 satırları toplayıp sütun başına tek değer bırakır.

title: The report is a chain of steps you can explain
meaning: The sensor project joins reading, validation, grouping, summarising and writing. Each step must say what input it accepts, what output it gives, and what it does on failure. A final average that looks reasonable does not prove that the whole chain is correct.
picture: Draw the pipeline and follow four rows through it: T1=10, T1=20, T1=missing and T2=30. Use matching units and values that the sensor rules allow. Keep accepted and rejected counts beside the flow.
predict: What should T1’s count and mean be? Can sorting, dropping duplicates or replacing the missing value with zero quietly change the answer?
steps: Validation accepts the three numeric rows and rejects the missing one with a reason.
T1 has count 2, sum 30 and mean 15; T2 has count 1 and mean 30.
A hand summary of these tiny inputs checks the output of the full pipeline.
answer: Keep the raw data. Report each sensor’s count separately from the total accepted-row count. Repeated equal readings may be real observations. Explain what happens when every row is invalid. Reopen the saved report and check it.
transfer: AA asks the next question. Can repeated per-sensor scans and a single-pass dictionary give exactly this same result, and how does their work grow? That comparison is optional here. CP1 first makes the program behave reliably.
tr: Her aşamanın girdi, çıktı ve hata kuralını belirt. Küçük veriyi elle özetleyerek bütün hattı kontrol et; makul görünen sonuç tek başına kanıt değildir.
